authoritativeBasis.materialsAndAssemblies: No free primary source exists at the required granularity — this is a PURCHASE, not a research task. RSMeans (Gordian), the reference standard for unit costs, crew composition, labour-hours per assembly and city cost indexes: https://www.rsmeans.com/ . Lower-cost alternative with a published annual edition: Craftsman National Construction Estimator, https://www.craftsman-book.com/ . BOTH ARE LICENSED PRODUCTS whose figures may not be redistributed as raw data — resolve the licensing question BEFORE building an ingestion path.
authoritativeBasis.labour: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) is the authoritative, free, citable basis for regional labour rates. Home: https://www.bls.gov/oes/ . National estimates: https://www.bls.gov/oes/current/oes_nat.htm . State and metro tables: https://www.bls.gov/oes/tables.htm . For this trade use SOC 47-2031 Carpenters.
authoritativeBasis.bls_NOT_captured: NO BLS WAGE FIGURES WERE CAPTURED in the 2026-08-15 pass. www.bls.gov returned HTTP 403 on every path attempted, via both the fetch tool and curl with a browser user-agent — the site is bot-blocking that environment. No median or mean hourly wage is recorded here, because recording one without having fetched it is the exact failure this pass exists to prevent. Retrieve from a different network or via the BLS public API with VERIFIED series IDs. OEWS is a MAY-REFERENCE ANNUAL SERIES — record the release year alongside every figure.
authoritativeBasis.oewsIsNotABillableRate: OEWS reports EMPLOYEE WAGES, not BILLABLE CONTRACTOR RATES. The gap between them (payroll burden, insurance, overhead, profit) is a multiplier currently folded into taughtDefaults. Document that relationship explicitly when real data lands, or the labour side will be wrong by a large and consistent factor while looking rigorously sourced.
